actual_record_replay.assessment: This is an exact source-recompiled wrapper-transparency lockstep regression. The reference and DUT datapath both instantiate the same R1 RTL source, so it is not an independent cycle or data oracle.

pinned_prior_r1_oracle.role: independent binary/address/signed reconstruction evidence for the unchanged R1 datapath, not an R3 FSM cycle oracle

findings.title: The FSM counts 128 descriptor accepts but does not enforce the 16-pattern by 8-block identity set or order
findings.evidence: The independent VCS bench sent pattern=0/block=0 128 times. All 128 descriptors were accepted and the phase retired without protocol_error. RTL state advances only on descriptor_count_q and carries no seen bitmap or expected pattern/block state.
findings.impact: A scheduler omission, duplicate, or permutation can silently replace required work while satisfying the phase bound. Exact production replay is safe only under an external trusted-scheduler assumption.
findings.minimal_fix: Freeze and assert the external descriptor-order assumption in the contract, or enforce expected (pattern,block) sequence/uniqueness in RTL and fail closed on duplicate, missing, or out-of-order identities.

findings.title: The phase FSM is functionally complete but intentionally serializes 460-row LOAD, COMMIT, 128-descriptor EXECUTE, and DRAIN
findings.evidence: The wrapper has one bank image and prohibits payload forwarding in COMMIT/EXECUTE/DRAIN. The contract explicitly excludes double buffering, LOAD/EXECUTE overlap, module speedup, and system speedup.
findings.impact: R3 closes liveness and phase-accounting defects but does not improve the inherited loader-dominated module throughput or re-admit an accelerator performance claim.
findings.minimal_fix: For performance work, add a terminal-row-aware ping-pong payload store or a producer-consumer prefetch boundary and measure complete phase cycles in the cycle simulator, including fill, drain, fallback, and stalls.

findings.title: The 1728-phase actual-record differential is not an independent datapath oracle
findings.evidence: The DUT wrapper and reference both instantiate sync_banked_guarded_pwp_frontend from rtl_m86/sync_banked_guarded_pwp_frontend.sv and receive the same legal streams and output_ready.
findings.impact: The test strongly detects wrapper-induced cycle differences, but a bug shared by both R1 instances can pass. The separately pinned prior R1 oracle mitigates data/address risk but is not an R3 cycle oracle.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep the lockstep label, pin the prior R1 independent oracle as done here, and add a scoreboard driven from sealed binary records for output and issue timing if R3 itself is called independently verified.

findings.title: The LOAD triple-contention progress assertion is not safely qualified for an OOB or duplicate payload on the attack edge
findings.evidence: The assertion requires payload_load_ready whenever all valids are high in LOAD and disables only when protocol_error is already high. A newly presented fail-closed OOB/duplicate can be rejected before protocol_error becomes visible on the following state update.
findings.impact: Binding the production SVA during negative fault attacks can flag correct fail-closed behavior, which is why the independent fault campaign cannot use this property unchanged.
findings.minimal_fix: Qualify progress with a legal payload row/not-seen predicate or split legal progress and illegal-request fail-closed properties.

findings.title: EXECUTE triple progress proves selection only and the generic bound omits accepted_descriptors <= 128
findings.evidence: ap_execute_triple_contention_progress concludes descriptor_selected, not ready/accept or bounded eventual acceptance. ap_fsm_bounds checks fsm_state and accepted_rows only.
findings.impact: Directed simulation covers the intended path, but the SVA layer does not itself prove descriptor acceptance progress or the exported descriptor counter bound.
findings.minimal_fix: Add accepted_descriptors<=128 and a ready/accept or bounded-liveness property under explicit downstream fairness assumptions.

findings.title: Held next-loader progress is conditional on downstream output_ready eventually releasing DRAIN
findings.evidence: The independent test holds DRAIN for six cycles and observes loader acceptance three cycles after output_ready release. With indefinite backpressure, r1_busy can remain asserted and LOAD is unreachable.
findings.impact: The measured bounded waits of 8 and 3 cycles are scenario-specific rather than unconditional starvation bounds.
findings.minimal_fix: State the output-ready fairness assumption beside the loader bound and measure the wait from the release/last-output event, not from an unconstrained request arrival.

findings.title: Reset destructively flushes in-flight bank/FIFO work
findings.evidence: The boundary campaign reset from partial LOAD, three FAULT classes, and DRAIN without ghost output. The DRAIN reset deliberately ended with 767 issues and 766 responses because one in-flight response was discarded.
findings.impact: This is a valid reset policy, but issue/response/output conservation properties must be disabled or re-based across reset; reset does not preserve accepted work.
findings.minimal_fix: Document destructive reset semantics and assert conservation only within reset-free epochs.

scoped_go: GO for replacing R2 arbitration with the explicit LOAD/COMMIT/EXECUTE/DRAIN/FAULT protocol for ordered legal traffic.
GO for exact 460-row uniqueness/boundary handling, 128-accept count, finite-drain handoff, sticky fault, and destructive reset behavior under the tested assumptions.
GO for R3 wrapper transparency relative to the unchanged R1 datapath over all 1728 actual phases and 221184 descriptors.
no_go: NO-GO for claiming descriptor schedule integrity unless the trusted ordered producer assumption is frozen or enforced.
NO-GO for calling the R3 actual differential an independent cycle/data oracle by itself.
NO-GO for double buffering, LOAD/EXECUTE overlap, real escape fallback, compiled SRAM, Synopsys PPA, module/system speedup, FPS, energy, DATE, or best-paper headline.

required_next_gate: Freeze or enforce the 128-entry descriptor identity/order contract.
Repair the negative-request and descriptor-bound SVA gaps.
Use a terminal-row-aware ping-pong or prefetch mechanism if the next milestone targets performance rather than control correctness.
Retain fail-closed claim separation until complete phase cycles, real fallback, macros, and Synopsys evidence exist.
